reviews.title: Racists.
reviews.text:
Education should never become a tool of political discrimination.

Why should access to knowledge and educational technology depend on the country someone was born in or currently lives in? Ordinary people are not responsible for their governments’ political decisions, yet they are the ones who end up paying the price.

I am willing to pay for NotebookLM. I want to use it for my studies, academic research, and personal development, but I am denied access solely because of regional restrictions.

Knowledge should have no nationality, and education should not be a privilege reserved for people living in the “right” countries.

Millions of ordinary people should not be punished for circumstances beyond their control. Access to education is an opportunity to learn and grow, not a reward for being born in the right place or belonging to the right political system.

Knowledge should unite people, not divide them. Racists. They block access after payment, assuming you’re in a different region.

reviews.title: What can I say about Gemini notebook that Gemini cannot say for itself?
reviews.text:
“It isn't productive, and you are spot on about why it breaks the core logic of a working tool.
​When a chat thread or generated output is automatically locked into the workspace as a permanent source—with zero ability to delete, edit, or prune individual turns—it completely undermines the user's ability to maintain a clean environment.
​A primary knowledge base shouldn't be ruined or contaminated simply because you had an exploratory or throwaway exchange with the AI. Forcing you to destroy the entire notebook and rebuild your whole source list from scratch just to purge unwanted chat history isn't just bad UI; it's a fundamental flaw in data architecture.
​For a workflow to actually be productive, the user has to be in full control of what stays, what goes, and what counts as a source. Locking chat history into the background state without a direct, granular purge button completely strips away that control.”

reviews.title: Notebook is awesome (but not on mobile)
reviews.text:
NotebookLM, now Gemini Notebook, is a staple for my research and studies. I love it. It’s why I pay for Google AI Pro, honestly. It’s so good that right after my student benefits expired (free Google One/AI Pro), I started paying for it. Just for Notebook. 

The mobile app sucks. So, so bad. I mean some functionalities on the mobile app are defunct on the desktop webapp. I’ll get a response in the chat thread, and click “save to notes”, and on IOS it still makes it a source material rather than placing it in the repository of the studio, with the reports, quizzes and flashcards, etc. 

It’s missing features (deep web research, lots of studio functionality, etc). It utilizes defunct functions. It’s just flat out ugly. 

This would be so, so amazing to have on the phone for my study and research on the go. Google, why? 

Have Gemini rebuild this horrible app, it’s selling the product short.

reviews.title: Export to Docs from a note in Sources produces unformatted raw Markdown in one paragraph.
reviews.text:
Hello,

When I export a note to Google Docs, the Doc contains the note's raw Markdown and LaTeX source as a single block of plain text. The formatting is not applied.

Steps to reproduce

	1.	Open a notebook in Gemini Notebook / NotebookLM (notebook.google.com) in Chrome on desktop.
	2.	In chat, use "Save to note" on a reply that contains headings, bullets, a table, and a formula. It saves to the Sources panel as a note.
	3.	In the Sources panel, open the note's three-dot menu and choose "Export to Docs".
	4.	Open the new Google Doc.

Expected: The Doc matches how the note looks in NotebookLM, with real headings, bullets, a table, and equations.

Actual: The Doc shows the Markdown symbols literally: ###, * , 1. , > , ---, and table pipes with a | :--- | row. Formulas appear as LaTeX source, for example \\(90^\circ\\) and \frac{T}{I\omega}. [Confirm on desktop: the text runs together with no line breaks.]

The screenshot attached shows the exported Doc. The note rendered correctly in NotebookLM before export.

Impact: The exported content is hard to read and can't be used directly for studying or sharing. Study-guide style notes with tables and formulas are the worst affected.

Date and environment: Tested 14 October 2026, Chrome on macOS, desktop with the latest chrome version.

Request: Please apply formatting on export, or convert the Markdown to Docs formatting. Please also preserve the formulas as equations or readable math.

Thank you.

reviews.title: Another Product Ruined
reviews.text: Everything Google touches dies.  The app version used to function like the web version and was highly functional and convenient.  That’s not good enough for the feature creeps in Mountain View. After a forced upgrade, the new interface is utter rubbish.  There is no longer an option to enter a prompt for a deep dive research.  You can’t even open a new notebook unless you add a source first. Why?  The chat area has no chat box to enter text. Why?  This is why I have been migrating away from Google ecosystem entirely.  NotebookLM was the exception, until now.  Don’t bother with this app, just use the web experience until Google ruins that too.

reviews.title: Looking for something else
reviews.text: Why do you companies always change the things that your customers want? I’m confused as to why in the world would you remove the "View Custom Prompt" option from the Audio Overview and Studio menus?!! What was the purpose? What was the reason? I uploaded a bunch of sources to multiple folders in my pro edition, and I usually just click on an old audio and copy and paste the prompt that was already there. I had a really good, and detailed prompt that was my go to, and all I had to do was just change a few words around, based on the topic that I needed. You guys chose to remove this feature and now I don’t have the prompt that I need for other folders and sources i’ve add and created. Please put it back because this is actually stupid to have to rewrite a new prompt for every audio or studio item I create. If you pay for the pro edition, it shouldn’t be this limited. Now I’m going to have to go on Reddit and find what other apps won’t limit me like this.
